bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Regulatory compliance risk — New regulations or amendments across multiple jurisdictions may create compliance risk if the Company fails to integrate the required processes; mitigated by continuous monitoring and interaction with regulatory authorities.
- Intense competition — Existing and emerging players in the industry may cause pricing pressure and impact profitability; the Company relies on innovation, quality standards and delivery efficiency to remain competitive.
- Intellectual property risk — As an API manufacturer, the Company faces risk of potential patent/copyright infringement disputes, which could lead to legal disputes and financial liabilities.
- Supply chain disruption — Dependence on globally sourced raw materials and international markets exposes the Company to disruptions from geopolitical, logistical or regional challenges; mitigated by diversifying geographic presence, product portfolio and supplier base.
- Product liability and safety risk — Products are used in pharmaceutical manufacturing to treat various diseases; any quality or safety failure could lead to liability claims and reputational damage.
- Economic and political instability — The Company imports raw materials and exports products internationally; economic disruption or political instability in key supplier/customer regions could adversely impact operations.
- Technological change — Rapid technological and industry-standard changes require sustained R&D investment; failure to adopt new technologies and innovate consistently could erode competitiveness.
- Currency and foreign exchange exposure — Significant international revenue exposure (imports of raw materials, exports of products to global markets) leaves the Company exposed to currency and forex fluctuations.

business.body:

- Integration is the stated moat: management commentary calls it "a differentiated, integrated organization — one that combines robust R&D, manufacturing capabilities, and a growing portfolio of novel and complex products", allowing the company "to capture value across the chain".
- CDMO positioning slide claims "'Clone-to-vial' capabilities makes us a preferred one-stop outsourcing partner", "One of the very few CDMO companies from India having integrated CDMO Biologics offerings" and "One of the very few CDMO companies from India having One Stop Solutions for Integrated CDMO offerings in ADCs"; a peer grid benchmarks Shilpa against 3 Indian and 3 global CDMOs across small molecule, peptide, mAb/recombinant, ADC and fermentation.
- Positioned as "a partner of choice for novel therapy development", with the deck citing four partnerships for novel assets, the latest being Gate2Brain.

business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Partnership — Orion] Partnership with Orion Corporation on two fronts: co-development and exclusive supply of a nivolumab biosimilar for Europe (Orion handles commercialization; Shilpa earns development, regulatory milestone and long-term supply revenue), and Orion as exclusive partner for distribution, marketing and sales of Shilpa's Recombinant Human Albumin for therapeutic use in Europe, with Shilpa entitled to development and regulatory milestone payments.
- [Partnership — Gate2Brain] Fourth partnership for a novel asset: Shilpa takes a stake in Gate2Brain and becomes its integrated CMC, manufacturing and regulatory partner for G2B-002, a BBB-penetrant, FDA & EMA Orphan Drug-designated oncology asset for brain cancer, with first-in-human trials targeted by FY28.
- [Regulatory setback — OLC/Unicycive] "The FDA issued CRL for its resubmitted OLC NDA, driven solely by unresolved third-party manufacturing deficiencies at FDF site (not related to clinical efficacy/safety of the product), as the FDA had not yet inspected the vendor's facility during the review"; approval is "expected in the near-term, pending resubmission of NDA". Shilpa is the exclusive CDMO partner and its milestone income spans filing, approval and launch stages.
- [Licensing — LatAm] "Entered into a strategic licensing agreement to commercialize a high value biosimilar across 30+ Latin American countries — Shilpa's first entry into the region", with an FY28-FY29 horizon.
- [Partners — NBE] Novel MAB (oncology) development with mAbTree targeting clinical trials in late FY27, with Orphan Drug Designation from the US FDA for Essential Thrombocythemia and Polycythemia Vera; a Novel Live Biotherapeutic Product development and manufacturing contract signed with Alveolus Bio; both Alveolus and mAbTree NBE projects expected to enter Phase 1 in FY27.

outlook.body:
- Three structural growth opportunities outlined for FY27 and beyond: the novel and complex formulations market, the global biosimilars wave, and the expanding CDMO outsourcing trend
- Deepening vertical/captive integration between the API and finished-dosage Formulations businesses, described as a deliberate and defining element of the operating model that is margin-accretive and reduces exposure to external pricing pressure
- Building and scaling a full-service Hybrid CDMO platform offering integrated end-to-end capabilities across small molecules, biologics, peptides, ADCs and GLP-1 under a single platform
- Systematic oncology API portfolio renewal, adding high-value molecules targeting patent expiries through 2032 to keep the pipeline commercially relevant into the next decade
- Scaling Noduca (NorUDCA) aggressively across India while advancing international regulatory submissions to build a multi-geography franchise on its global first-mover NAFLD-treatment status
- Converting the CDMO clinical-stage pipeline into commercial programmes, a transition expected to accelerate through FY27 and FY28 as multiple programmes reach commercialisation milestones
- Advancing the Biologics pipeline (Aflibercept, Recombinant Human Albumin, Novel Biological Entities) from clinical/regulatory stages toward submission and commercial launch
- The Board recommended a final dividend of Rs 0.60 per equity share (60% of face value of Rs 1) for FY26, to be put to shareholder vote at the 39th AGM. During the year the Company also completed a 1:1 bonus share issue (allotted 6 October 2025), returning value to shareholders through both dividend distribution and capital-base expansion rather than a buyback.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The API business (Shilpa Lifesciences, Raichur, Karnataka) is expanding a new dedicated oncology manufacturing block, targeted for commissioning by end of FY27 to add capacity for existing and new oncology API products. A dedicated, fully automated peptide manufacturing facility is under construction; equipment for a large-scale peptide manufacturing block was ordered during FY26, laying the groundwork for capacity addition in FY27, alongside completed Semaglutide process validation ahead of DMF filing. During FY26 the Company completed capacity expansion for UDCA (production consolidated into a single manufacturing site) and Tranexamic Acid (batch size enhancement), and undertook batch size scale-ups and process optimisation across several oncology molecules (Ibrutinib, Enzalutamide, Nilotinib, Bortezomib, Temozolomide), freeing manufacturing capacity within existing blocks for new molecules. New molecule validations were completed for Palbociclib, Olaparib and both forms of Ruxolitinib (oncology) and Mycophenolate Mofetil and a CDCA intermediate (non-oncology). Two new manufacturing blocks were added during the year, taking total API capacity to 11 Non-Oncology Blocks (~682KL) and 10 Oncology Blocks (~238KL) at the Raichur Unit-1 & Unit-2 facilities. In Specialty CDMO, a dedicated OLC manufacturing block was commissioned during FY26 and the ADC GMP facility received its Test License from Indian regulatory authorities. An import-substitute non-oncology API completed process validation, with commercial revenues expected to begin from FY27; Teduglutide completed laboratory development with process validation expected to complete in H1 FY27; for GLP-1, one product's DMF is ready while Semaglutide's DMF filing is targeted for H1 FY27. In Polymers, an ophthalmic polymer proof-of-concept was completed with repeat orders received from a multinational client. Separately, the Company stated it invested ₹361 crores during the year on its ongoing expansion programme along with maintenance capex.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's domestic pharmaceutical market is at an inflection point, driven by rising healthcare expenditure, expanding insurance coverage and growing incidence of non-communicable diseases across oncology, metabolic and chronic therapeutic categories
- Physicians and healthcare systems are increasingly receptive to novel, clinically differentiated therapies rather than generic alternatives alone, creating headroom for companies with genuine R&D capabilities to build durable domestic franchises
- A large number of high-value biologic medicines face patent expiry across major markets over the next five to seven years, and healthcare systems in the US, Europe and emerging economies are actively seeking biosimilar alternatives; regulatory frameworks in key markets have matured, providing a clearer approval pathway
- Global pharmaceutical and biotech companies are restructuring supply chains, seeking trusted, quality-assured CDMO partners for complex modalities including biologics, peptides, ADCs and advanced drug delivery systems
- India's combination of regulatory credibility, scientific depth, manufacturing scale and cost competitiveness positions it as the destination of choice for global CDMO partnerships
- A substantial portion of manufacturing infrastructure, particularly in Biologics, CDMO and novel delivery systems, remains in early stages of utilisation, providing meaningful operating leverage as volumes scale
- Specialty CDMO (API CDMO, Peptide & Polymer) active pipeline of 25+ programmes
- CDMO NCE pipeline: first US NCE programme transitioned to commercial launch with a global pharmaceutical partner; second programme approaching its PDUFA date with commercialisation anticipated post regulatory approval; third programme undergoing Phase III trials
- OLC programme with Unicycive Therapeutics flagged as the most immediate CDMO commercialisation milestone
- Biologics pipeline: Aflibercept in Phase III trials in India, Nivolumab commencing Phase I human studies, Recombinant Human Albumin programme with Orion Corporation (initial milestone payment received, Phase III planned across India and Europe in FY27), Novel Biological Entities with mAbTree and Alveolus Bio on track for Phase I human trials in FY27
- Portfolio strengthened with four new biosimilar programmes added: Nivolumab, Pembrolizumab, Daratumumab and Dupilumab
- Strategic licensing agreement signed with SteinCares for commercialisation of a biosimilar across 30+ Latin American countries
- Formulations pipeline includes 505(b)(2) programmes for US markets described as meaningful near-term growth opportunities

currentContext.expansion: The API business (Shilpa Lifesciences, Raichur, Karnataka) is expanding a new dedicated oncology manufacturing block, targeted for commissioning by end of FY27 to add capacity for existing and new oncology API products. A dedicated, fully automated peptide manufacturing facility is under construction; equipment for a large-scale peptide manufacturing block was ordered during FY26, laying the groundwork for capacity addition in FY27, alongside completed Semaglutide process validation ahead of DMF filing. During FY26 the Company completed capacity expansion for UDCA (production consolidated into a single manufacturing site) and Tranexamic Acid (batch size enhancement), and undertook batch size scale-ups and process optimisation across several oncology molecules (Ibrutinib, Enzalutamide, Nilotinib, Bortezomib, Temozolomide), freeing manufacturing capacity within existing blocks for new molecules. New molecule validations were completed for Palbociclib, Olaparib and both forms of Ruxolitinib (oncology) and Mycophenolate Mofetil and a CDCA intermediate (non-oncology). Two new manufacturing blocks were added during the year, taking total API capacity to 11 Non-Oncology Blocks (~682KL) and 10 Oncology Blocks (~238KL) at the Raichur Unit-1 & Unit-2 facilities. In Specialty CDMO, a dedicated OLC manufacturing block was commissioned during FY26 and the ADC GMP facility received its Test License from Indian regulatory authorities. An import-substitute non-oncology API completed process validation, with commercial revenues expected to begin from FY27; Teduglutide completed laboratory development with process validation expected to complete in H1 FY27; for GLP-1, one product's DMF is ready while Semaglutide's DMF filing is targeted for H1 FY27. In Polymers, an ophthalmic polymer proof-of-concept was completed with repeat orders received from a multinational client. Separately, the Company stated it invested ₹361 crores during the year on its ongoing expansion programme along with maintenance capex.

risks.note: New regulations or amendments across multiple jurisdictions may create compliance risk if the Company fails to integrate the required processes; mitigated by continuous monitoring and interaction with regulatory authorities.
Existing and emerging players in the industry may cause pricing pressure and impact profitability; the Company relies on innovation, quality standards and delivery efficiency to remain competitive.
As an API manufacturer, the Company faces risk of potential patent/copyright infringement disputes, which could lead to legal disputes and financial liabilities.

Dependence on globally sourced raw materials and international markets exposes the Company to disruptions from geopolitical, logistical or regional challenges; mitigated by diversifying geographic presence, product portfolio and supplier base.
Products are used in pharmaceutical manufacturing to treat various diseases; any quality or safety failure could lead to liability claims and reputational damage.
The Company imports raw materials and exports products internationally; economic disruption or political instability in key supplier/customer regions could adversely impact operations.
Rapid technological and industry-standard changes require sustained R&D investment; failure to adopt new technologies and innovate consistently could erode competitiveness.
Significant international revenue exposure (imports of raw materials, exports of products to global markets) leaves the Company exposed to currency and forex fluctuations.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's domestic pharmaceutical market is at an inflection point, driven by rising healthcare expenditure, expanding insurance coverage and growing incidence of non-communicable diseases across oncology, metabolic and chronic therapeutic categories
- Physicians and healthcare systems are increasingly receptive to novel, clinically differentiated therapies rather than generic alternatives alone, creating headroom for companies with genuine R&D capabilities to build durable domestic franchises
- A large number of high-value biologic medicines face patent expiry across major markets over the next five to seven years, and healthcare systems in the US, Europe and emerging economies are actively seeking biosimilar alternatives; regulatory frameworks in key markets have matured, providing a clearer approval pathway
- Global pharmaceutical and biotech companies are restructuring supply chains, seeking trusted, quality-assured CDMO partners for complex modalities including biologics, peptides, ADCs and advanced drug delivery systems
- India's combination of regulatory credibility, scientific depth, manufacturing scale and cost competitiveness positions it as the destination of choice for global CDMO partnerships
- A substantial portion of manufacturing infrastructure, particularly in Biologics, CDMO and novel delivery systems, remains in early stages of utilisation, providing meaningful operating leverage as volumes scale
- Specialty CDMO (API CDMO, Peptide & Polymer) active pipeline of 25+ programmes
- CDMO NCE pipeline: first US NCE programme transitioned to commercial launch with a global pharmaceutical partner; second programme approaching its PDUFA date with commercialisation anticipated post regulatory approval; third programme undergoing Phase III trials
- OLC programme with Unicycive Therapeutics flagged as the most immediate CDMO commercialisation milestone
- Biologics pipeline: Aflibercept in Phase III trials in India, Nivolumab commencing Phase I human studies, Recombinant Human Albumin programme with Orion Corporation (initial milestone payment received, Phase III planned across India and Europe in FY27), Novel Biological Entities with mAbTree and Alveolus Bio on track for Phase I human trials in FY27
- Portfolio strengthened with four new biosimilar programmes added: Nivolumab, Pembrolizumab, Daratumumab and Dupilumab
- Strategic licensing agreement signed with SteinCares for commercialisation of a biosimilar across 30+ Latin American countries

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The API business (Shilpa Lifesciences, Raichur, Karnataka) is expanding a new dedicated oncology manufacturing block, targeted for commissioning by end of FY27 to add capacity for existing and new oncology API products. A dedicated, fully automated peptide manufacturing facility is under construction; equipment for a large-scale peptide manufacturing block was ordered during FY26, laying the groundwork for capacity addition in FY27, alongside completed Semaglutide process validation ahead of DMF filing. During FY26 the Company completed capacity expansion for UDCA (production consolidated into a single manufacturing site) and Tranexamic Acid (batch size enhancement), and undertook batch size scale-ups and process optimisation across several oncology molecules (Ibrutinib, Enzalutamide, Nilotinib, Bortezomib, Temozolomide), freeing manufacturing capacity within existing blocks for new molecules. New molecule validations were completed for Palbociclib, Olaparib and both forms of Ruxolitinib (oncology) and Mycophenolate Mofetil and a CDCA intermediate (non-oncology). Two new manufacturing blocks were added during the year, taking total API capacity to 11 Non-Oncology Blocks (~682KL) and 10 Oncology Blocks (~238KL) at the Raichur Unit-1 & Unit-2 facilities. In Specialty CDMO, a dedicated OLC manufacturing block was commissioned during FY26 and the ADC GMP facility received its Test License from Indian regulatory authorities. An import-substitute non-oncology API completed process validation, with commercial revenues expected to begin from FY27; Teduglutide completed laboratory development with process validation expected to complete in H1 FY27; for GLP-1, one product's DMF is ready while Semaglutide's DMF filing is targeted for H1 FY27. In Polymers, an ophthalmic polymer proof-of-concept was completed with repeat orders received from a multinational client. Separately, the Company stated it invested ₹361 crores during the year on its ongoing expansion programme along with maintenance capex.

themes.title: Pharma US complex-generics & specialty exports
themes.need: US complex generics, Para-IV FTFs and the GLP-1/semaglutide wave still drive export pharma, but Q1FY27 delivered one hard setback and one deliberate trough. DRREDDY held an out-of-cycle call disclosing a semaglutide injectable API scale-up validation failure - an out-of-spec impurity in finished product - halting supply through roughly September and re-cutting FY27 volumes to 6-7 million pens (Q3-Q4) from an earlier ~12mn first-year target, which re-times India's largest semaglutide launch and opens a share window for rivals. CIPLA let EBITDA margin fall to 16.7%, below the pre-Revlimid level, because launch opex is committed ahead of revenue plus ~1-2% of revenue in war-related input cost - yet reaffirmed BOTH an FY27 18.5-20% margin and a $1bn US exit run-rate off a $162m Q1, making this a trough by design with unusually large operating leverage if the launches land. The GLP-1 opportunity is bifurcating: CIPLA's Yurpeak (tirzepatide, Eli Lilly collaboration) did INR 80cr and is already the #2 anti-obesity brand behind Mounjaro while Cipla deliberately sits out the crowded semaglutide-generic price war. NATCOPHARM remains in a gRevlimid post-cliff base year; LUPIN/ALKEM/ZYDUSLIFE/LAURUSLABS carry cleaner momentum; SENORES/MARKSANS on US generics; DIVISLAB on GLP-1 peptides (55% CDMO mix).
themes.driver: DRREDDY's semaglutide supply restart (guided ~September) and whether the 6-7mn-pen re-cut holds; CIPLA's four US launches landing against the reaffirmed 18.5-20% FY27 margin; FTF launches and USFDA clearances; DIVISLAB Kakinada Unit 3 from FY27.
